title: Lowbit fidelity scan playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a lightweight, operational playbook for running a low-bit fidelity scan across a set of candidate models and workloads. The goal is not perfect science but to surface signal quickly: where 4-bit / INT8 / FP8 produce acceptable quality vs where they introduce regressions that matter to product. Use this as a reproducible checklist + minimal spreadsheet template for stakeholders (SRE, infra, applied-ml, product).

When to use this playbook:
- You have 2–4 candidate model variants (e.g., base-7B, 13B, 70B) and want per-route recommendations.
- You need a quick before/after on quality metrics (ROUGE/EM/F1/QA-acc) plus token-latency and unit-cost estimates.
- You want to prioritize quant knobs by ROI (cost savings vs observable quality drop).

High-level approach:
1) Define 3 representative workload buckets: short-shot (<32 tokens), mid-shot (32–256 tokens), long-shot (>256 tokens). Use real production trace samples where possible.
2) For each model variant and bucket, run microbench for throughput and p99 token latency for FP32 (baseline), FP8, INT8, and 4-bit.
3) Run small eval set (200–1,000 prompts per bucket) for quality signals. Prefer task-specific metrics and a simple hallucination detector when applicable.
4) Produce a single-row summary per (model, bucket, quant) with: metric_delta, p99_latency_ratio, tokens/sec, cost_per_1M_tokens_est, notes.
5) Use heuristic rules (below) to produce per-route recommendations.

Minimal spreadsheet layout (one row per variant/bucket/quant):
- model_name | bucket | quant | tokens_sec | p99_ms | cost_1M_tokens_usd | metric_baseline | metric_quant | metric_delta_pct | recommended_action | rationale

Example sample rows (text form, paste into sheet):
base-7B | short | FP32 | 5200 | 18 | 4.32 | QA_acc: 0.87 | QA_acc: 0.86 | -1.1 | keep | tiny degradation, no cost win
base-7B | short | INT8 | 7500 | 22 | 2.99 | QA_acc: 0.87 | QA_acc: 0.86 | -1.1 | trial | lower cost, small latency increase, run A/B
base-7B | long | 4-bit | 640 | 120 | 3.10 | F1: 0.62 | F1: 0.47 | -24.2 | avoid | catastrophic loss on long context

Notes on metrics and thresholds (team input):
- Metric delta sensitivity:
  - Green: delta <= 1.5% relative (acceptable for UI chat or suggestions)
  - Yellow: 1.5% < delta <= 5% (worth A/B + guardrails)
  - Red: delta > 5% (do not use in production for this route)
- Latency sensitivity by route: conversational chat: p99 <= 120ms target, document-summarization: p99 <= 600ms, batch embedding: throughput > 8k tokens/sec preferred.

Heuristic decision rules (operational):
- If cost_savings >= 30% and metric_delta <= 1.5% -> recommend canary on 10% traffic with logging of hallucination rate + fallback to FP32 after 3 regressions per 1k requests.
- If metric_delta in (1.5%, 5%] and latency improves materially (>15% p99 reduction) -> recommend A/B test using route-level gating and quality monitoring.
- If metric_delta > 5% -> do not deploy. Consider hybrid: use low-bit for prefix caching or for candidate reranking only, not for final generation.

Practical microbench commands (example harness snippets we use):
- run_token_bench --model base-7b --dtype fp32 --batch-size 8 --seq-len 256 --out metrics/base-7b-fp32-short.csv
- run_token_bench --model base-7b --dtype int8 --batch-size 8 --seq-len 256 --out metrics/base-7b-int8-short.csv
- quality_eval.py --prompts workloads/short-200.json --model base-7b --dtype int8 --out eval/base-7b-int8-short.json

Practical gotchas and observational checks:
- Quantized KDE: 4-bit often collapses rare-token distributions. Watch top-k token-prob entropy and rare entity recall specifically.
- KV cache mismatch: some low-bit kernels reduce effective KV cache speed due to extra memory ops; measure end-to-end p99 with real request fanout.
- Batch packing differences: low-bit runtimes may allow larger effective batches; account for real traffic shape when extrapolating tokens/sec.
- Validation leakage: if eval prompts are too similar to fine-tune data, false positives for quality. Use held-out real traces when possible.

Quick ROI estimator (text pseudo-formula to put into a sheet cell):
- cost_per_1M_tokens = (gpu_hour_cost_usd / (tokens_sec * 3600)) * 1e6
- relative_cost_savings_pct = 100 * (1 - cost_quant / cost_fp32)
- p99_latency_ratio = p99_quant / p99_fp32

Operational checklist before canary: (short)
- [ ] Run microbench for target seq distribution and measure tokens/sec + p99.
- [ ] Run quality eval with at least 200 prompts across buckets.
- [ ] Add alerts: metric_falloff > 1.5% and hallucination_rate > baseline + 0.5% -> auto-rollout-fail.
- [ ] Add tracing to correlate latencies with cold/warm tokens and cache hits.
- [ ] Prepare rollback playbook (route-level pin to FP32, revoke canary, notify owners).

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Which product routes are tolerant of a 2–3% QA drop in exchange for 40% cost savings? (assign to Priya)
- Automate the microbench -> sheet ingestion so the summary row is generated by CI (assign to Evan).
- Investigate hybrid strategies that keep final beam in FP32 while doing draft scoring in 4-bit (assign to Jonah).

Appendix: small sample outputs to paste into a sheet (CSV-friendly):
model,bucket,quant,tokens_sec,p99_ms,cost_1M_tokens_usd,metric_baseline,metric_quant,metric_delta_pct
base-7B,short,fp32,5200,18,4.32,QA_acc:0.87,QA_acc:0.87,0.0
base-7B,short,int8,7500,22,2.99,QA_acc:0.87,QA_acc:0.86,-1.15
base-7B,mid,fp32,2100,46,10.70,ROUGE-L:0.42,ROUGE-L:0.42,0.0
base-7B,mid,fp8,2600,58,8.65,ROUGE-L:0.42,ROUGE-L:0.40,-4.76
base-7B,long,4bit,640,120,3.10,F1:0.62,F1:0.47,-24.19

Contact / ownership notes:
- Primary owner: Marisol Vega (product-optimize).
- Bench infra and automation: Evan Cho (eng-tools).
- Quality evaluation owner: Priya Nair (applied-ml).

If this playbook is useful, next iteration should add: automated CI snippet to upload microbench CSVs to the shared sheet, regression alert templates, and a short training notebook to reproduce failure modes for rare-entity collapse.
